title: A Front Divided
subtitle: The campaign’s situation at the close of Phase II
author: R.G. Cruise
phase: II — The Drive into the Soviet Interior
summary: Planned study: The three sectors, Soviet resistance, supply and replacement problems, occupation violence and the developing southward operations.
outlineTopics: Army Group North's position and progress toward Leningrad.
Soviet resistance and defensive preparations in the northern sector.
The status of the Baltic campaign and continuing fighting around Tallinn.
Army Group Center's advances and the operational consequences of the Smolensk fighting.
The continued existence of organized Soviet resistance east of Smolensk.
German and Soviet losses, using verifiable figures with properly defined date ranges.
Army Group South's position following Uman.
The Soviet defensive situation in Ukraine.
The German decision to redirect operational effort toward the south.
The developing German movement toward the Desna and the next stages of the Ukraine campaign.
Logistical problems, supply distances, repair requirements, and replacement shortages.
Soviet mobilization, reserve formations, and operational adaptation.
The expansion of German occupation administrations and the escalating murder of civilians, particularly Jewish communities.
Why the invasion had not achieved its original objective of destroying Soviet resistance within a short campaign.
researchStatus: Editorial outline established; full narrative, document locators and the dated military situation require research.
referenceMapStatus: Collection reference only. The corresponding printed sheet date, sheet identifier and reuse conditions have not yet been verified.
chronologyNotes: This is the editorial endpoint of Phase II; it does not end the broader Battle of Smolensk or import September operations.
